com: Behold a Lamb, by which is divers times represented our Saviour Christ. (Witham)

They sung as it were a new canticle. In these visions, after persecutions, are sometimes introduced rejoicings to encourage the servants of God in their sufferings from the wicked world. — No man could say (or sing) the canticle, but those hundred and forty-four thousand: by which are signified the elect, who were not defiled with women. Some expound this literally of those who always lived virgins; others understand all those who lived or died with a pure and clean heart, exempt from the corruption of vices, and of whom it is said, (ver. 5) that in their mouth was found no lie, and that they were without spot for the throne of God. (Witham)

These are they, &c. In the style of the prophets, by fornication is meant idolatry, and virginity signifies cleanness from all sacrilegious worship. These, therefore, are virgins in this sense, who have not fallen into the impurities of creature worship. But others, as St. Augustine, understand it of persons who have lived in continency. The first, however, is the more literal sense. (Calmet)
Another Angel,…saying: Fear the Lord.[1] By this Angel are represented the preachers of the gospel, exhorting all men to the true faith and a good life. (Witham)

Another Angel,…saying:…She is fallen, she is fallen, that great Babylon. By Babylon, as observed before, may very probably be signified all the wicked world in general, whom God will punish and destroy after the short time of this mortal life: or may be signified every great city, and perhaps Rome returned to idolatry in the time of antichrist, a little before the end of the world, or may be signified the idolatry of heathen Rome, in the fourth age[century], when the Christian religion, under Constantine and his successors, began to triumph over paganism, i.e. according to those interpreters followed by Alcazar, Bossuet, P. Alleman, &c. which exposition Dr. Hammond thus expresseth: “the whole impure city of heathen Rome, under the title of Babylon, that old idolatrous city that had lain so heavy upon the people of God….should speedily be destroyed, for advancing the heathen worship.” (Witham) — It is probable that here by the great Babylon is meant the city of the devil; that is, the universal society of the wicked: as Jerusalem is taken for the city and the Church of God. (Challoner)

The third Angel followed….if any man shall adore the beast,…he also shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is mingled with pure wine, &c. That is, he shall drink of the bitter cup of God’s indignation, not mixed with water, or any thing to diminish its force, but with wine and wine; i.e. with punishments upon punishments for ever and ever. (Witham)

Here is the patience of the saints. Here patience is necessary, so as not to be carried away with such pleasures and vanities as are offered in the wicked Babylon, and to remain firm under persecutions with the pious inhabitants of Jerusalem. (Witham)

Blessed are the dead (all the dead) who die in the Lord, and not the martyrs only, for their works follow every one. (Witham) — It is understood of the martyrs, who die for the Lord. (Challoner) — For their works follow them. It is just that they rest at length from their labours, and enjoy for eternity the recompense of their fidelity. They land on the shores of their native country, enriched with the treasures of the good works they have done in this lower world. This is said in express contradiction to those who denied the necessity of good works, and maintained the indifference of actions. This seems to have been the doctrine of the Nicolaites and other heretics of those times. (Calmet) — The Holy Ghost confirms the sentence of their happiness, not only because at the moment of their departure their hard labours and penitential works cease, but their souls are admitted to a glorious immortality, the recompense of their good works. (Pastorini)

Like to the Son of man. That is, to our Saviour Christ, sitting on a white cloud, with a crown of gold, and in his hand a sharp sickle. And another Angel, desiring of him to do justice, by putting in his sickle, because the harvest of the earth was ripe, dry, and withered; i.e. the wicked, ripe for punishment. The like is again represented by the sickle, which is said to be put to the clusters of the vineyard: and they were cast into the great wine-press, or lake of the wrath of God, into hell, where the blood is said to come out even up to the horses’ bridles, for a thousand and six hundred furlongs: a metaphorical way of expressing the exceeding great torments of the wicked in hell. But to pretend form hence to give the just dimensions of hell, is a groundless conjecture; of which see Cornelius a Lapide. (Witham)

Babylon.... By Babylon may be very probably signified all the wicked world in general, which God will punish, and destroy after the short time of this mortal life: or it may signify every great city wherein enormous sins and abominations are daily committed; and that when the measure of its iniquities is full, the punishments due to its crimes are poured on it. It may also be some city of the description in the text, that will exist, and be destroyed, as here described, towards the end of the world.
Die in the Lord.... It is understood of the martyrs who die for the Lord.
fa: Treatise 12. Three Books of Testimonies Against the Jews
Treatise XII Three Books of Testimonies Against the Jews

… But ye shall not touch any one upon whom the sign is written, and begin with my holy places themselves. Also in Exodus God says to Moses: "And there shall be blood for a sign to you upon the houses wherein ye shall be; and I will look on the blood, and will protect you. And there shall not be in you the plague of wasting when I shall smite the land of Egypt. Also in the Apocalypse: "And I saw a Lamb standing on Mount Sion, and with Him a hundred and forty and four thousand; and they had His name and the name of His Father written on their foreheads. …
Commentary on Revelation

And I saw, and behold, a Lamb was standing upon Mount Zion. If we carefully inspect the text of the following reading, we will see that the things said about the one hundred and forty‑four thousand belong rather to the elect, whose souls rejoice with the Lord in heavenly blessedness, than to those who toil in this life. Therefore the Lamb represents Christ; and Zion is interpreted as “watchtower” or “lookout”; by the mountain of Zion we must understand the heavenly homeland. Therefore, on Mount Zion the Lamb was seen, because in heavenly blessedness Christ abides with his saints.
Commentary on Revelation

And with him were one hundred and forty‑four thousand, having his name and the name of his Father written on their foreheads. In the third vision which goes before this one, it is said that one hundred and forty‑four thousand from the twelve tribes were chosen and marked with the sign of faith. That one hundred and forty‑four thousand, therefore, as the explanation of the names of the twelve tribes shows, refers to the elect who work in this life; but this one hundred and forty‑four thousand signifies the elect who rejoice with the Lord in heavenly glory, as the text of the present reading plainly signifies. …
Commentary on Revelation

And I heard a voice from heaven, like the voice of many waters, and like the voice of great thunder. Often through John the faithful of the present life are shown; by waters, however, peoples are signified. And because from all nations the elect are daily gathered and placed in heavenly blessedness, the holy ones of God established on earth, who are signified through John, constantly hear the voice of many waters; because they perceive with the ears of the heart the teaching of the saints who dwell in heaven, and, with whatever strength they can, imitate their actions. …
Commentary on Revelation

And the voice that I heard was like the voice of harpists playing on their harps. The voice of harpists is exceedingly sweet to those who hear; and what is sweeter to the faithful than the remembrance of the saints dwelling in heaven, while they ponder in their minds how great their glory is, and humbly pray that they may someday achieve it?
On the Resurrection of the Flesh

If I remember not that it is I who have served Him, how shall I ascribe glory to God? How sing to Him "the new song," if I am ignorant that it is I who owe Him thanks? But why is exception taken only against the change of the flesh, and not of the soul also, which in all things is superior to the flesh? How happens it, that the self-same soul which in our present flesh has gone through all life's course, which has learnt the knowledge of God, and put on Christ, and sown the hope of salvation in this flesh, must reap its harvest in another flesh of which we know nothing? …
Commentary on Revelation

I have said what I felt. But if anyone should wish to apply the text of this reading to the present Church, and to understand by the one hundred and forty‑four thousand either the preachers or the other righteous people still living in this life; and to judge that by the new song, which no one could sing except those alone, the Gospel is indicated; let such a person consider that the holy Gospel is preached not only by the elect, but also very often by the wicked, about whom we believe the Lord to have said in the Gospel: …
Commentary on Revelation

… Therefore, in the sight of the faithful, who are signified by the throne and the four living creatures and the elders, the souls of the faithful are said to have sung a new song; because holy men, placed on this earth, continually behold with the eyes of the mind the glory of the saints dwelling in heaven, and that they may some day come to their fellowship, they strive with all their strength. And no one could sing the song except those one hundred and forty-four thousand who were redeemed from the earth; that is, none of those who are signified by the throne and the four living creatures and the elders. …
Treatise 12. Three Books of Testimonies Against the Jews
Treatise XII Three Books of Testimonies Against the Jews

… Also in Exodus, when the Lord had commanded Moses that he should sanctify the people for the third day, he sanctified them, and added: "Be ye ready, for three days ye shall not approach to women. Also in the first book of Kings: "And the priest answered to David, and said, There are no profane loaves in my hand, except one sacred loaf. If the young men have been kept back from women, they shall eat. Also in the Apocalypse: "These are they who have not defiled themselves with women, for they have continued virgins; these are they who follow the Lamb whithersoever He shall go."
On Prayer

Equally in each sex let the younger age follow the discipline of the elder; or else let the male "virgins," too, be veiled, if the female virgins withal are not veiled, because they are not mentioned by name.
Commentary on Revelation

These are those who have not been defiled with women; for they are virgins. Here again a question arises; for if in that blessedness there are different ranks, such as apostles, martyrs, confessors, and virgins, how is it that all the souls of the saints are said to be virgins, and so virgins that they are said not to have been defiled with women? And if what the Lord says is true, indeed it is true, since it cannot happen that God should lie: “Whoever looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart”, (Matt. …
Commentary on Revelation

They follow the Lamb wherever he goes. Where does he go who fills all things and is wholly present everywhere? But the Apostle teaches how he goes, saying: “He has mercy on whom he wills, and he hardens whom he wills” (Rom. 9:18). God therefore “goes” by having mercy on some and withdrawing his mercy from others. The saints in truth follow, because to those on whom he grants his mercy, they also grant it; and from those from whom he cuts it off, they also cut it off. …
Commentary on Revelation

They have been redeemed from among all people as first fruits for God and the Lamb. In the Law it is commanded that the first fruits of the crops be offered to God (Exod. 22:29); by the first fruits of the crops, the elect are signified. For just as from the multitude of fruits a small portion of first fruits was offered to God, so from the multitude of peoples a small number of elect is chosen, who are offered by the angels to God in the temple of heavenly glory, as the Lord says in the Gospel: “For many are called, but few are chosen” (Matt. 22:14). …
Commentary on Revelation

… Therefore it does not seem to me that this statement is made about every kind of lie, but there is a very serious kind of lying, when we lie about the things that we promised in baptism. This, then, is the lie that was not found in the mouth of the saints; because they endeavored to keep, to the very end of life, what they had promised in baptism. And even if there were some who after baptism committed many sins, yet no lie was found in their mouth; because through penance and works of love they strove to wipe out before death the evil they had done: for they are without stain. …
Treatise 11. Exhortation to Martyrdom, Addressed to Fortunatus
Treatise XI Exhortation to Martyrdom Addressed to Fortunatus

… In the Apocalypse, moreover: "And I saw another angel fly in the midst of heaven, having the everlasting Gospel to preach over the earth, and over all nations, and tribes, and tongues, and peoples, saying with a loud voice, Fear God rather, and give glory to Him: for the hour of His judgment is come; and worship Him that made heaven and earth, and the sea, and all that therein is. So also the Lord, in His Gospel, makes mention of the first and second commandment, saying, "Hear, O Israel, The Lord thy God is one God; " and, "Thou shalt love thy Lord with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength. …
Commentary on the Apocalypse of the Blessed John

"And I saw an angel flying through the midst of heaven." The angel flying through the midst of heaven, whom he says that he saw, we have already treated of above, as being the same Elias who anticipates the kingdom of Anti-christ in his prophecy.
Commentary on Revelation

And I saw another angel flying in mid-heaven, having an eternal Gospel, to preach to those who sit upon the earth, and to every nation, and tribe, and tongue, and people, saying with a loud voice. Again he briefly sums up everything; for just as above, when he wished to relate the evils of Antichrist, he began from the coming of Christ, and, first recounting the persecutions which the Church has suffered from the Devil, came at last to Antichrist; so also here, wishing to describe the Day of Judgment, he begins from the coming of Christ, and, under the figure of three angels, briefly going over everything, reaches the Day of Judgment. …
Commentary on Revelation

Fear the Lord, and give Him honor; for the hour of His judgment has come, and adore Him who made heaven and earth, the sea and the springs of waters. Fittingly he placed the fear of the Lord first, and afterward honor; for the fear of the Lord drives a person to repentance, and repentance in turn urges him to perform good works. Therefore we pay honor to God when we do good works, just as the Lord Himself says: “Let your good works be seen, and let them glorify your Father who is in heaven” (Matt. 5:16). Now the hour of judgment began from the moment the Gospel started to be preached. …
Commentary on Revelation
And worship him who made heaven and earth, and the sea and the springs of waters; That is, leave behind the deaf, mute, and blind idols, and worship him who made all things out of nothing.
Commentary on the Apocalypse of the Blessed John
"And another angel following him." The other angel following, he speaks of as the same prophet who is the associate of his prophesying.
Commentary on Revelation
And another angel followed, saying. Another angel signifies the doctors of the Church, who, when the persecutions had ended, governed the Church of God.
Commentary on Revelation

Fallen, fallen is great Babylon. By Babylon, as we said above, the city of the Devil is signified, which is made up of all the ungodly. Now it had fallen because every practice of demons had been destroyed through faith in Christ. And it is said to have fallen twice, because it fell both on the side of the persecutors and on the side of diabolic worship.
Commentary on Revelation

She made all nations drink from the wine of her wrath. The wine of wrath is the errors of the pagans, by which they provoked God to anger. But since Babylon is nothing other than all the nations, that is, all the wicked, how did she make all nations drink from the wine of her wrath? In truth, since one taught another, and that one a third, and the third a fourth, and therefore the demonic error passed into all men, Babylon certainly made all nations drink the wine of the wrath of God.
Treatise 11. Exhortation to Martyrdom, Addressed to Fortunatus
Treatise XI Exhortation to Martyrdom Addressed to Fortunatus

… In the Apocalypse too: "If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead or in his hand, he shall also drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is mixed in the cup of His wrath, and shall be punished with fire and brimstone before the eyes of the holy angels, and before the eyes of the Lamb: and the smoke of their torments shall ascend for ever and ever: and they shall have no rest day or night, whosoever worship the beast and his image."
Treatise 12. Three Books of Testimonies Against the Jews
Treatise XII. Three Books of Testimonies Against the Jews.

… Also in the same place: "And the third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice, If any man worship the beast and his image, and hath received his mark in his forehead or upon his hand, the same shall drink of the wine of His wrath, and shall be punished with fire and sulphur, under the eyes of the holy angels, and under the eyes of the Lamb; and the smoke of their torments shall ascend up for ever and ever."
Commentary on Revelation

And the third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice: If anyone worships the beast and its image, and receives its mark on his forehead or on his hand, he too will drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is mixed with the unmixed in the cup of Him. The third angel are the preachers who are to come in the times of Antichrist; for they will preach that no one should worship Antichrist, nor bend the ears of the heart to his worst teaching, nor imitate his works; and they will bear witness that if anyone does this, he is to be condemned to everlasting punishment.
Commentary on Revelation

… By “unmixed,” therefore, the justice of God is signified, and by “cup” we can understand the judgment of God. Therefore the wine is mixed with what is unmixed in the cup of God, because the final damnation by which the wicked will be condemned will be mingled with justice in the cup of God, that is, in the judgment of God; for it will be brought to completion by the most just judgment of God. The wicked will therefore drink the wine of the wrath of God, when it is said to them: Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire, which has been prepared for the Devil and his angels (Matt. 25:41).
Commentary on Revelation

And he will be tormented with fire and sulfur in the sight of the holy angels and in the sight of the Lamb; and the smoke of their torments will rise forever and ever. Fire burns, but sulfur gives off a most terrible stench. With fire they will be physically tormented, those who were unwilling to extinguish within themselves the fire of vices; they will be tortured by the stench of sulfur, for whom the stench of lust was sweet. …
Commentary on Revelation

And they will have no rest day or night, those who have worshiped the beast and its image, and whoever receives the mark of its name. Why does he say that the wicked will have no rest either by day or by night, since the elect are to possess an eternal day, and the wicked an everlasting night? But he spoke in a human manner.
Commentary on Revelation
This is the patience of the saints, who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus. That is, such is the patience of the saints, and it brings forth such fruit as is shown in what follows.
Commentary on Revelation

And I heard a voice from heaven saying to me: Write, “Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord.” Such therefore is the patience of the saints, who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus, that they may be blessed forever. But what is it that he says: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord? For who, being dead, can die? Surely no dead person can die, unless he first receives back his soul, so that he can die again. …
Commentary on Revelation

From now on, says the Spirit, that they may rest from their labors. “From now on,” that is, from the time of their death, the saints will rest from their labors. For their works follow them. How do they follow? Did not the works of Cornelius go before him, to whom it was said by the angel: “Your prayers and your alms have been remembered in the sight of God” (Acts 10:4)? But he used “follow” with the meaning “to accompany”; for an army that accompanies the king is also said to follow him, though some go before, some follow behind, and some march at his right or left. …
Commentary on Revelation

And I saw, and behold, a white cloud, and upon the cloud one sitting like the Son of Man, having on his head a golden crown, and in his hand a sharp sickle. And another angel went out from the temple, crying with a loud voice to him who sat upon the cloud, saying: Send forth your sickle, and reap; for the hour has come to reap, since the harvest of the earth has dried up. And he who sat upon the cloud sent his sickle into the earth, and reaped the earth. And another angel went out from the temple, which is in heaven, having also himself a sharp sickle. …
Commentary on the Apocalypse of the Blessed John

"Thrust in thy sharp sickle, and gather in the grapes of the vine," he signifies it of the nations that should perish on the advent of the Lord. And indeed in many forms he shows this same thing, as if to the dry harvest, and the seed for the coming of the Lord, and the consummation of the world, and the kingdom of Christ, and the future appearance of the kingdom of the blessed.
Commentary on Revelation

Another angel who came out of the temple cried with a loud voice to him who was sitting upon the cloud, saying: “Put in your sickle, and reap”; he points out the elect who labor on this earth, but by the temple from which he was seen to have come out, the Church is indicated. …
Treatise 12. Three Books of Testimonies Against the Jews
Treatise XII Three Books of Testimonies Against the Jews

… And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do anything unto him: for now I know that thou fearest thy God, and hast not spared thy beloved son for my sake. Also in the second Psalm: "Serve the Lord in fear, and rejoice unto Him in trembling. Also in Deuteronomy, the word of God to Moses: "Call the people together to me, and let them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me all the days that they themselves shall live upon the earth. Also in Jeremiah: "Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will perfect upon the house of Israel, and in the house of Judah, a new covenant: …
Commentary on Revelation

Similarly, the fourth angel who came out from the altar, who had power over the fire, has the same meaning as the second, who was seen to have come out of the temple; for he signifies the elect who labor in this life. The altar, however, signifies the Church, just as the temple does; and by the fire we can understand love, which the Holy Spirit, through spiritual kindling, nourishes in the hearts of the saints. The saints are therefore said to have power over this fire because they both possess love and are possessed by it. …
Commentary on the Apocalypse of the Blessed John

"And the angel thrust in the sickle, and reaped the vine of the earth, and cast it into the wine-press of the wrath of God. And the wine-press of His fury was trodden down without the city. In that he says that it was cast into the wine-press of the wrath of God, and trodden down without the city, the treading of the wine-press is the retribution on the sinner. "And blood went out from the wine-press, even unto the horse-bridles. The vengeance of shed blood as was before predicted, "In blood thou hast sinned, and blood shall follow thee." "For a thousand and six hundred furlongs. …
Commentary on Revelation

And the winepress was trodden outside the city. By the treading, we can understand the plunging of the wicked down into hell [infernum]; by the city, however, is signified the heavenly Jerusalem, which is made up of all the chosen. Therefore the winepress will be trodden outside this city, because the wicked will be separated from the fellowship of the righteous and thrust down into hell [infernum], as the Lord says in the Gospel: The angels will go out and will separate the evil from among the righteous, and will cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth there (Matt. 13:49–50).
Commentary on Revelation

And blood came out of the lake as far as the horses’ bridles, for one thousand six hundred stadia. By the blood, the punishment of the wicked is signified; by the distance of one thousand six hundred stadia, which the blood coming out of the lake occupied, false Christians are signified: for although this number is derived from the number four, it is nevertheless spread everywhere, always keeping the same number, and does not leap beyond its boundaries. …
ftr: John Litteral, released into the public domain
